title: Open-cover sheaf dg Hom sequence and derived scalar naturality
statement:
Fix universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $X$ be a topological space with a sheaf $\mathcal S$ of commutative rings and a sheaf dg $\mathcal S$-algebra $\mathcal C$. Use left dg modules, signed shifts and cones, and the localization $D_X(\mathcal C)$ of [def-sfb-sheaf-dg-module-localization]. Let $U,V\subseteq X$ be opens with $X=U\cup V$, and put $T=U\cap V$. For $P,Q\in D_X(\mathcal C)$ and any open $Z$ put
$$H_Z^n(P,Q)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D_Z(\mathcal C|_Z)}(P|_Z,(Q|_Z)[n])\qquad(n\in\mathbf Z).$$
There is a long exact sequence of abelian groups
$$\cdots\to H_U^{n-1}(P,Q)\oplus H_V^{n-1}(P,Q)\to H_T^{n-1}(P,Q)\xrightarrow{\partial}H_X^n(P,Q)\to H_U^n(P,Q)\oplus H_V^n(P,Q)\to H_T^n(P,Q)\xrightarrow{\partial}H_X^{n+1}(P,Q)\to\cdots.$$
The maps from $X$ are restriction and the maps to $T$ are difference of restrictions. The boundary is the one obtained by applying contravariant Hom into $Q[n]$ to the extension-by-zero triangle
$$j_{T!}(P|_T)\longrightarrow j_{U!}(P|_U)\oplus j_{V!}(P|_V)\longrightarrow P\longrightarrow j_{T!}(P|_T)[1].$$
Here $j_Z:Z\hookrightarrow X$ is inclusion, and $j_{Z!}$ is termwise extension by zero: its stalk is the given module stalk at points of $Z$ and zero outside $Z$, with the induced dg action. The first triangle map has the inclusion components with opposite signs and the second has the two counits as components. The sequence is natural contravariantly in $P$ and covariantly in $Q$.

For every map $\varphi:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C'$ of sheaf dg $\mathcal S$-algebras, put $L_\varphi=\mathcal C'\otimes_{\mathcal C}^{\mathbf L}-$, the derived extension of [lem-sfb-ringed-dg-scalar-adjunction], and use its canonical comparisons with open restriction and shifts. Applying $L_\varphi$ to morphisms gives a morphism from the displayed sequence to the sequence for $L_\varphi P,L_\varphi Q$ over $\mathcal C'$, including all boundary squares. These maps respect identity maps and composition of algebra maps with the canonical adjunction comparisons. No flatness, perfectness, quasi-coherence, boundedness or quasi-compactness hypothesis is imposed; empty opens are allowed.

source.place: Tag 08BW (lemma-mayer-vietoris-hom), extension-by-zero triangle proof; sheaf dg refinement using sdga.tex Tags 0FRW (lemma-extension-by-zero-dg) and 0FRX (lemma-tensor-with-extension-by-zero-dg). The dg scalar-extension boundary compatibility is an agent-formulated strengthening, not the assertion of Tag 08BW itself.

proof.text: For an actual left dg module $M$, put $A(M)=j_{T!}M|_T$ and $B(M)=j_{U!}M|_U\oplus j_{V!}M|_V$. The open-extension calculus defines natural dg maps $a=(\iota_{T,U},-\iota_{T,V}):A(M)\to B(M)$ and $b=(\varepsilon_U,\varepsilon_V):B(M)\to M$, with $ba=0$ by its counit coherence. In each degree apply [lem-sc-open-cover-mate-module-short-exact] to the underlying $\mathcal S$-module sheaf $M^r$ on the ringed space $(X,\mathcal S)$ and the ordinary extension/restriction adjunctions. Its maps are exactly these underlying maps, since both transpose the identity on the smaller open. Thus $0\to A(M)\xrightarrow a B(M)\xrightarrow b M\to0$ is degreewise short exact. The dg Grothendieck-category node computes kernels and cokernels on underlying graded sheaves, so this is also exact as dg modules. The stalk cases are the diagonal-with-minus followed by addition on $T$, and the identity sequence on $U\setminus V$ or $V\setminus U$; the cover excludes any fourth case.

Form the specified dg cone $C(a)=B(M)\oplus A(M)[1]$ and $q:C(a)\to M$, $q(b_0,a_0)=b(b_0)$. It is a dg map since $ba=0$. The cone-short-exact quasi-isomorphism node, applied to the underlying complexes of $\mathcal S$-module sheaves, makes $q$ a quasi-isomorphism; this is exactly the class inverted in the dg localization. The scalar-adjunction node gives the triangulated structure with the specified cone triangles. Replacing the third vertex of $A(M)\to B(M)\to C(a)\xrightarrow{-p}A(M)[1]$ by $M$ gives a distinguished triangle with boundary $\delta_M=-p q^{-1}$. A dg map $f:M\to M'$ gives the cone map $(B(f),A(f)[1])$; its compositions with $p$ and $q$ give $A(f)[1]\delta_M=\delta_{M'}f$. Since $A,B$ preserve homotopies and quasi-isomorphisms by the open-extension calculus, localization of natural transformations extends this identity to every derived morphism. Hence the triangle is natural in $P$, with the same signed boundary for any representative.

source.place: Tag 0FTB (lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor), cone formula and its naturality

proof.text: Apply contravariant Hom into $Q[n]$ to this triangle and all its rotations. The Hom-out-of-triangle exactness node gives exactness at each adjacent pair; rotating and shifting covers every integer. The additive open adjunctions identify $\operatorname{Hom}(j_{Z!}P|_Z,Q[n])$ with $H_Z^n(P,Q)$. Under them precomposition with $b$ is restriction, and precomposition with $a$ is restriction from $U$ minus restriction from $V$. If $\gamma:P|_T\to Q|_T[n-1]$ and $\widetilde\gamma:A(P)\to Q[n-1]$ is its adjunct, the connecting map is $\partial\gamma=\widetilde\gamma[1]\circ\delta_P$, using the coherent shift identifications. This fixes its sign. All terms are abelian groups since the category is additive. Naturality of the triangle in $P$, and postcomposition into $Q[n]$, prove the stated contravariance and covariance, including the boundary.

Fix $\varphi:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C'$ and abbreviate ordinary extension by $F$ and its derived functor by $L$. Choose a graded-flat homotopically flat resolution $H\to P$ using [lem-sfb-sheaf-dg-hflat-computation]. Restrictions of $H$ are again graded-flat homotopically flat: for an acyclic right module $T$ on $Z$, extend it by zero; [lem-sfb-sheaf-dg-open-tensor-projection] identifies $(j_!T)\otimes_{\mathcal C}H$ with $j_!(T\otimes_{\mathcal C|_Z}H|_Z)$, and restrict back to $Z$. The same argument with a short exact sequence of graded right modules proves graded flatness. Conversely, for graded-flat homotopically flat $G$ on $Z$, the other projection formula identifies $T\otimes j_!G$ with $j_!(T|_Z\otimes G)$; exactness of restriction and extension by zero proves both properties of $j_!G$. Consequently $H,A(H),B(H)$ have these properties. So does $C(a)$: its underlying graded module is $B(H)\oplus A(H)[1]$, and tensoring it with an acyclic right module is the signed cone of a map between acyclic complexes, hence acyclic by the cohomology long exact sequence. Thus the derived-to-ordinary comparisons $\epsilon$ are isomorphisms on all four objects.

source.place: Tags 0FRB, 0FRX; Tag 0FSH (lemma-resolve) and the definition of homotopical flatness

proof.text:
The tensor projection isomorphism with the $(\mathcal C',\mathcal C)$-bimodule $\mathcal C'$ identifies $F A(H),F B(H)$ with $A'(FH),B'(FH)$, carrying $Fa,Fb$ to the cover maps by counit compatibility. Here primes mean extension by zero for $\mathcal C'$. Tensor commutes with the signed cone: on a homogeneous tensor $c'\otimes(b_0,a_0)$ the cone comparison is $(c'\otimes b_0,(-1)^{|c'|}c'\otimes a_0)$. Inserting the tensor differential and the shifted left action gives exactly the cone differential and action. Hence $Fq$ is the cover cone map $q'$ and $Fp$ is $p'$ after this shift comparison. The right-Kan coherent-shift node makes $\epsilon_{A(H)[1]}=\epsilon_{A(H)}[1]\sigma_{A(H)}$, where $\sigma:L(A[1])\simeq (LA)[1]$. Naturality of $\epsilon$ for $p,q$, and invertibility of $q,q'$ and these comparison maps, therefore gives
$$\epsilon_{A(H)}[1]\sigma_{A(H)}L(-p q^{-1})=(-p'(q')^{-1})\epsilon_H.$$
This is the missing boundary square, not merely a comparison of the first two arrows. The isomorphisms on $H,A(H),B(H)$ consequently identify $L$ of the entire cover triangle with the cover triangle of $LP$. Independence of $H$ follows from the universal derived comparison and the open/scalar adjunctions: their comparison is the left-adjoint uniqueness map to the same right composite, so agrees with the canonical comparisons in the statement.

For each open $Z$, send $f:P|_Z\to Q|_Z[n]$ to $L_Z(f)$ followed by the shift comparison, using the restriction comparison to view its endpoints as $(LP)|_Z,(LQ)|_Z[n]$. This is additive. The first two arrow squares follow from the counit-compatible comparisons of step 5. For the boundary, apply $L$ to $\widetilde\gamma[1]\delta_P$. Step 5 replaces $L(\delta_P)$ by $\delta_{LP}$ and the shift of the comparison on $A(P)$; naturality of the shift comparison replaces $L(\widetilde\gamma[1])$ by $(L\widetilde\gamma)[1]$. Since the open adjunction comparison preserves counits, $L\widetilde\gamma$ is the adjunct of the image of $\gamma$. The resulting composite is precisely $\partial$ of that image. This proves every boundary square in every degree.

source.place: Tags 0FTR (lemma-derived-adjoint-push-pull), 0FRX; the explicit boundary formula of Tag 0FTB

proof.text: For two successive algebra maps, the right adjoints are restrictions and their composite is literally restriction along the composite. The canonical unit-compatible left-adjoint uniqueness isomorphism identifies the two successive derived extensions with extension along the composite. Its naturality gives the same map on every Hom group, and compatibility with the units and counits makes its open comparisons the ones already used. Associativity is exactly the left-adjoint-composition associativity node; the identity comparison is the uniqueness map to the identity adjunction. These comparisons commute with shifts because both composites have the shift comparison determined by the derived universal comparison. Thus identities and compositions respect the whole sequence and the boundary calculation. All constructions were unbounded and used flat resolutions over the dg algebra, never flatness of the algebra map or of the algebras over $\mathcal S$. If an open is empty its extension by zero and all its Hom groups are zero; the same formulas still apply.
